---
title: "Recipes"
---

Recipes are short task pages. Each recipe solves one task. Each recipe ends with a check you can run.
The recipes rise in difficulty. Recipe 1 installs Trishula on a local Docker provider and reads the first verdict.
Recipe 2 applies a WAFPolicy and reads the verdict line.
Recipes 3 to 8 carry the advanced lanes: verdicts, budgets, exclusions, bans, kernel maps, the bench.

## The recipe ramp

The table lists the planned ramp. Simple tasks sit first. Advanced tasks sit last.
A planned recipe stays PENDING until a worked pin and a smoke run exist.

| # | Recipe | Level | Feeds from |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Install Trishula on a kind cluster and see the first verdict | easy | [the DX1 lab path, `lab/dx1/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/lab/dx1) |
| 2 | Apply your first WAFPolicy: CR plus one curl, the verdict line | easy | [§11.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#113-cel-as-the-developer-facing-dsl), the CRD surface |
| 3 | Read the verdicts: the OTel record shape (`trishula.verdict.v1`) | easy | [§15.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#152-the-verdict-record-log-body-schema-versioned), the verdict signals |
| 4 | Write a CEL rule at S3 with a cost budget | medium | [§11.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#113-cel-as-the-developer-facing-dsl), [§8.1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#81-design-principles) |
| 5 | Tune the CRS exclusion set without dropping the reference posture | medium | [§11.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#112-crs-the-correctness-baseline), [§11.8](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#118-crs-differential-parity-gate) |
| 6 | Run the ban ladder: ScoredWindowBan shadow, then enforce | hard | [§13.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#133-the-ban-algorithm-scoredwindowban-v1-specified) |
| 7 | Pre-seed the kernel maps from the operator bundle | hard | [§16.4](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#164-lifecycle-of-trishula-in-a-cluster), the seed pack |
| 8 | Run the CRS differential and the bench harness on your own node | hard | [§11.8](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#118-crs-differential-parity-gate), [§17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#17-performance-targets--benchmark-plan) |

## The recipe form

Every recipe carries the same parts:

- A header strip table. The columns: Tool, Section, Level, Time, Layer, Tags.
- **Problem** — the task and its walls.
- **Solution** — numbered steps. Each step quotes a real command.
- **Discussion** — what the step did. What to watch. What to tune.
- **See also** — the linked surfaces.
- Expected output shows shapes and placeholders only. A recipe never prints an invented transcript.
- The provenance footer records the pin, the date and the smoke status.

Level is metadata: easy, medium or hard. Level never becomes a navigation layer.
The prose follows [ASD-STE100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Technical_English):

- One thought per sentence. 20 words at most.
- Active voice. Present tense. Approved verbs. Digits for numbers.
- Steps read imperative.

## Recipe 1 — Install Trishula on a kind cluster and see the first verdict

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/dx1/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/lab/dx1) on any Docker provider (kind, or OrbStack Kubernetes) | Getting started | easy | 15 min | gateway + engine | install, kind, verdict |

### Problem

You want Trishula on a local Kubernetes cluster. You want one enforced verdict on one probe request.
You want it inside the 15 min M3 gate window. You do not want a hosted cluster or manual manifests.

### Solution

You need docker, crane, helm, kubectl, go and curl. You need one Docker provider:
kind, or the OrbStack-provided Kubernetes.

1. Clone the product repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula && cd trishula
```

2. Run the timed DX1 gate. The gate builds the linux binaries, brings the lab up
and times the first enforced rule:

```bash
bash lab/dx1/dx1-gate.sh
```

3. Read the printed evidence. The shapes below come from the recorded run.
Volatile values stand as placeholders:

```text
== pre-policy baseline: the benign probe passes transparently (200)
== (d) effect: SQLi probe → 403
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
== M9 apply→effect: <ms> (target ≤ 5s) — PASS
== DX1 verify: hop 1 NGF -> hop 2 engine -> hop 3 echo pod all evidenced above
== Done. The lab remains installed (no teardown).
```

The gate asserts the verdict fields on the blocked probe: `X-Trishula-Decision: block`
and `X-Trishula-Rule: DX-LAB-001`. The probe answers 403.

4. The three legs run alone. Each leg is idempotent. The lab stays installed:

```bash
bash lab/dx1/setup.sh
bash lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh
bash lab/dx1/verify.sh
```

`setup.sh` reuses the cluster, rebuilds the engine image and re-applies the manifests.
`apply-effect.sh` applies the policy, compiles the bundle and times the apply→effect leg.
`verify.sh` prints the hop-by-hop evidence. Re-run any leg at any time.

### Discussion

The request path carries three hops:

```text
client ──> NGF edge-gateway ──> dx1-engine ──> dx1-echo
```

The engine hop marks its response with `X-Trishula-Hop: engine`.
A second Host value on the same NodePort skips the engine. The HTTPRoute steers only the engine host.

The apply leg applies the lab `WAFPolicy`. The operator compiles rule `DX-LAB-001` and publishes the bundle.
The engine picks up the bundle. No restart happens.
The SQLi probe is a POST with a UNION probe in the query string. The engine answers 403.
The benign POST still passes: `defaultAction: pass` keeps the transparent forward.

The M9 leg carries a 5 s budget. The recorded smoke read 1174 ms. The M3 budget is 15 min
from clone to first enforced rule. The gate fails above either budget.

A broken policy fails at compile. The operator publishes no bundle. The engine keeps the loaded bundle.
The traffic shape does not change. Both pods stay Ready.

On OrbStack-provider Kubernetes, the NGF 2.x dataplane does not register.
`setup.sh` then installs the NGF 1.6.2 single-pod chart. The hop evidence stays the same.

### See also

- [The DX1 lab README](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/dx1/README.md) — the three steps and the knobs.
- [spec §10.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#102-the-contract-trishula-as-a-gateway-api-citizen) — the Gateway API contract. [spec §10.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#103-the-reference-walkthrough-the-lab-every-claim-is-proven-in) — the reference walkthrough.
- [The Build page](building.html) — the same loop inside the site's verification story.
- [DX1 issue #6](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/6) · [TR-08c issue #76](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/76).

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@7c352f65](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/7c352f6510d12aea7769b726735b1aa107f105df)
on main, 2026-10-24.

Smoke run, 2026-10-24, on the OrbStack-provided Kubernetes provider with NGF 1.6.2:

- `lab/dx1/setup.sh`: exit 0. The marker `DX1 lab setup complete` printed.
- `lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh`: exit 0. The M9 leg read 1174 ms. The fail-closed leg read 8758 ms.
- `lab/dx1/verify.sh`: exit 0. The hop evidence printed.

The gate composes the same three legs. No separate gate run is recorded.

## Recipe 2 — Apply your first WAFPolicy: CR plus one curl, the verdict line

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh) | Getting started | easy | 2 min after Recipe 1 | policy + engine | policy, WAFPolicy, CEL, verdict |

### Problem

You have the lab from Recipe 1. You want one WAFPolicy CR to gate one route.
You want the verdict line on the response. You want the same verdict in the engine log.
You want the transparent requests to still pass.

### Solution

The lab stays up from Recipe 1. You need kubectl and curl.

1. Run the apply→effect leg. The leg applies the CRD and the lab policy.
The leg times the apply→effect round trip. The leg then runs the fail-closed scenario:

```bash
bash lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh
```

2. Read the printed evidence. The shapes below carry placeholders:

```text
== pre-policy baseline: the benign probe passes transparently (200)
== (b) t0 — kubectl apply dx1-wafpolicy.yaml
== effect: SQLi probe → 403
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
== M9 apply→effect: <ms> (target ≤ 5s) — PASS
== fail-closed scenario: <ms> from apply(broken) to the logged compile error; traffic unchanged; pods Ready
```

3. Gate one probe with one curl. The shapes below come from the recorded run.
Volatile fields stand as placeholders:

```bash
NODE_IP=$(kubectl get nodes -o go-template --template '{{range .items}}{{range .status.addresses}}{{if eq .type "InternalIP"}}{{.address}} {{end}}{{end}}{{end}}' | awk '{print $1}')
curl -s -i -X POST "http://${NODE_IP}:31437/v1/chat/completions?q=UNION%20SELECT%2F%2A" \
  -H "Host: dx1-routed.dx1.example.com"
```

The blocked probe answers 403 and carries the verdict line:

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Trishula-Decision: block
X-Trishula-Hop: engine
X-Trishula-Rule: DX-LAB-001

blocked by DX-LAB-001
```

4. Check the benign request. The default action keeps the transparent forward:

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST "http://${NODE_IP}:31437/v1/chat/completions?q=greeting" \
  -H "Host: dx1-routed.dx1.example.com"
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Trishula-Decision: pass
X-Trishula-Hop: engine
```

### Discussion

The policy CR declares `defaultAction: pass` and one rule set.
The rule set points at the rule pack. The pack sits in a ConfigMap (`dx1-sqli`) in the policy namespace.
The pack carries one CEL rule:

```text
request.method == "POST" &&
path.matches("/v1/chat/*") &&
request.query.contains("UNION")
```

The operator compiles the rule into the bundle. The engine picks up the bundle. No restart happens.
The response carries the verdict vocabulary: `pass` and `block`. The blocked response names the rule id.
The engine log carries the same verdict line:

```text
engine: decision block (rule=DX-LAB-001) for POST /v1/chat/completions
```

The apply→effect leg carries the 5 s M9 budget. The gate fails above the budget.
A broken policy fails at compile. No bundle ships. The traffic shape does not change. Both pods stay Ready.
A bad CR keeps the last good decisions. That is the fail-closed posture.

### See also

- [spec §11.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#113-cel-as-the-developer-facing-dsl) — the CEL rule surface.
- [The WAFPolicy CRD](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/manifests/crd/wafpolicy-crd.yaml) · [The lab policy](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/deployment/dx1/manifests/dx1-wafpolicy.yaml) · [The rule pack](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/deployment/dx1/manifests/dx1-rulepack-sqli.yaml).
- [TR-08c issue #76](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/76) — the apply→effect gate.
- [The DX1 lab README](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/dx1/README.md) — the three steps and the knobs.
- Recipe 1 above — the install path.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the OrbStack-provided Kubernetes provider with NGF 1.6.2:

- The verdict curls: the benign POST read 200 with `X-Trishula-Decision: pass`. The SQLi probe read 403 with `X-Trishula-Decision: block` and `X-Trishula-Rule: DX-LAB-001`.
- The engine log carried the same decision line.

## Recipe 3 — Read the verdicts: the OTel record shape (`trishula.verdict.v1`)

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/trishula`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/trishula), one command, any host with Go | Observability | easy | 5 min | engine · observability | verdicts, otel, parity |

### Problem

You want the verdict record fields. You want the action, the rule ids and the score per case.
You want them without a dashboard or a cluster.

### Solution

1. Walk the ladder parity matrix. One command from a checkout:

```bash
go run ./cmd/trishula --parity
```

2. Read the printed verdict log. The three matrix cases carry the verdict vocabulary:

```text
verdict log (parity walk, S0+S3 slice):
  case clean      action=allow    rules=[]                 score=0 [PASS]
  case cel-match  action=log      rules=[TR02-001]         score=1 [PASS]
  case kernel-ban action=ban      rules=[shield:ban:t2:r7] score=2 [PASS]
parity OK
```

3. Read the record schema at [spec §15.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#152-the-verdict-record-log-body-schema-versioned).
The record carries six fields: `request.id`, `verdict.action`, `verdict.phase`, `verdict.route`,
`verdict.rules`, `verdict.score`.

### Discussion

The pipeline emits three correlated signals per verdict (TR-11): one span, one `verdicts_total`
datapoint, one log record. One request id keys all three signals. The log record
carries the event name `trishula.verdict` and an INFO severity. The signals are the
record's source; the spec pins the schema. The parity walk prints the same
verdict vocabulary the record carries.

The v0 pipeline emits in-process, into an in-memory exporter. No collector and no
network exporter ship at this pin. The parity walk is the reader surface.

### See also

- [spec §15](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#15-opentelemetry-observability) — the observability contract. [spec §15.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#152-the-verdict-record-log-body-schema-versioned) — the record schema.
- [`internal/engine/otel/pipeline.go`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/internal/engine/otel/pipeline.go) — the signal schema in code.
- [TR-11 issue #11](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/11) — the verdict pipeline.
- Recipe 1 above — the install path.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the host clone:

- `go run ./cmd/trishula --parity`: exit 0. The matrix read 3/3 `[PASS]` and printed `parity OK`.

## Recipe 4 — Write a CEL rule at S3 with a cost budget

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/trishula`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/trishula) + a rule pack file, any host with Go | Policy | medium | 10 min | engine · cel | cel, cost budget |

### Problem

You want one CEL rule at the S3 slot. You want a hard cost ceiling on it.
You want proof the ceiling bites, at evaluation and at compile.

### Solution

1. Copy the seed pack to a work file. Declare a budget below the rule's real cost
(the seed rule evaluates at cost 3):

```yaml
rules:
  - id: R4-BUDGET
    name: rate-shape-budget-bite
    description: 'The seed rate rule under a 2-cost ceiling'
    action: log
    costBudget: 2
    expression: |
      request.method == "POST" &&
      path.matches("/v1/chat/*") &&
      request.rate_windows["5m"].requests > 40
```

2. Run the pack. The ceiling stops every evaluation:

```bash
go run ./cmd/trishula --selftest --rules <pack-path>.yaml
```

```text
case below-threshold-no-match             match=false error=true  cost=3     FAIL detail=operation cancelled: actual cost limit exceeded
exit status 1
```

3. Check the compile side. The bundle load refuses an unusable declared budget
(the fail-closed gate):

```bash
go test ./internal/operator -run TestLoadRejectsUnusableDeclaredBudget -count=1
```

```text
ok   github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/internal/operator  <seconds>s
```

### Discussion

The budget rides the pack wire: `costBudget` sits on the rule. The policy's
`celBudget` is the fallback ceiling. Rule budget wins. A budget change re-plans
the program; it never re-compiles the module. The refusal detail names the
ceiling: `actual cost limit exceeded`. The compile-side gate rejects a pack whose
rule cannot run under its declared budget. No bundle ships on refusal.

The rule rides the S3 slot: the same rate rule the parity walk prints at S3.

### See also

- [spec §11.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#113-cel-as-the-developer-facing-dsl) — the CEL DSL. [spec §8.1](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#81-design-principles) — the cost-budget principle.
- [The seed pack](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/rules/cel/seed.yaml) — the rule form.
- [TR-17 issue #17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/17) — hot reload + cost budgets.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the host clone:

- `go run ./cmd/trishula --selftest --rules <pack-budget-2>.yaml`: exit 1. Every case read
  `error=true cost=3` with `detail=operation cancelled: actual cost limit exceeded`.
- `go test ./internal/operator -run TestLoadRejectsUnusableDeclaredBudget -count=1`: ok.

## Recipe 5 — Tune the CRS exclusion set without dropping the reference posture

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`test/crs-differential`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/test/crs-differential), any host with Go | CRS | medium | 15 min | crs · differential | crs, exclusions, parity |

### Problem

You want to silence one noisy CRS rule for one target. You want the community
baseline intact after the edit. You want a gate that catches drift.

### Solution

1. Read the committed exclusion set. The private ids `990001` to `990004` carry it
(`990001` = the response-body plumbing; the other three = the removals):

```text
SecRule REQUEST_FILENAME "!@rx ^/$" "id:990002,phase:1,pass,nolog,ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById=941010;REQUEST_FILENAME"
SecRule TX:DETECTION_PARANOIA_LEVEL "@ge 1" "id:990003,phase:1,pass,nolog,ctl:ruleRemoveById=921170"
```

2. Run the parity gate. The baseline against the committed set:

```bash
go test ./test/crs-differential/ -run TestCorpusParity -count=1
```

```text
parity 19/19 ran (1 skipped; target >= 90%) — zero unexplained deltas = gate
```

3. Probe the gate. Disable one exclusion (comment out id `990002` in
`test/crs-differential/testdata/seclang/engine.conf`) and run the gate again.
The gate fails and names the deltas:

```text
--- FAIL: TestCorpusParity/01-clean-post (0.00s)
    runner_test.go:61: parity delta: 941010 demotion evidence: want false, reference true
parity 13/19 ran (1 skipped; target >= 90%) — zero unexplained deltas = gate
```

4. Restore the edit. The gate reads green again.

### Discussion

The exclusion set lives as SecLang control rules with private ids. The ids sit
outside the CRS ranges: CRS parity semantics pin by includes and removes, never
by renumbering CRS. The corpus pins the observed rule-id sets per request. The
gate fails on any drift the edit introduces. Exclusion `990002` removes rule `941010` from the `REQUEST_FILENAME` target. Disabling it lets `941010` demote case evidence. The gate names the delta per case.

Tune by ids. Run the gate after every edit. The reference posture = the corpus
reading green at the pinned target.

### See also

- [spec §11.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#112-crs-the-correctness-baseline) — the correctness baseline. [spec §11.8](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#118-crs-differential-parity-gate) — the differential parity gate.
- [The differential README](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/test/crs-differential/README.md) — the corpus and the delta table.
- [TR-07 issue #7](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/7) — CRS integration.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the host clone:

- Baseline gate: parity 19/19 ran (1 skipped), zero unexplained deltas, ok.
- Probe with id `990002` disabled: parity 13/19, FAIL, three named `941010 demotion evidence` deltas.
- Restore: parity green again. The tree reads clean after restore.

## Recipe 6 — Run the ban ladder: ScoredWindowBan shadow, then enforce

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/demo-attack.sh`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/demo-attack.sh), Linux VM, root, BTF | Enforcement | hard | 20 min | kernel · bans | bans, tc, TC_ACT_SHOT |

### Problem

You want the ban path end to end on a Linux node. You want the scored window as the shadow input. You want one ban row in the kernel map. You want the attacker source dead.

### Solution

1. Build the demo binary. Place the flow object; it ships committed:

```bash
cp test/tier/tier_probe_arm64_bpfel.o /tmp/flow_tc.o   # arm64; x86: tier_probe_x86_bpfel.o
go build -o /tmp/attackdemo ./cmd/attackdemo
```

2. Give the harness an HTTP target for its wire legs. A plain HTTP server on the
same port answers them:

```bash
printf '#!/bin/sh\nIP="${1%%:*}"; PORT="${1##*:}"\nexec python3 -m http.server --bind "$IP" "$PORT"\n' > /tmp/tfo
chmod +x /tmp/tfo
```

3. Run the demo (root, Linux, kernel 5.15+, BTF present):

```bash
sudo env DEMO_BIN=/tmp/attackdemo ./lab/demo-attack.sh
```

4. Read the shadow legs, then the enforcement leg:

```text
bola:     object=2002 owner=tenant-b subject=tenant-a → BLOCK (API1:2023 BOLA)
cel:      GET /api/v1/orders/2002 rate=1/5m → match=false cost=3
ban:      [10.99.0.66] family=4 class=0 tier=1 reason=4211 until=mono+120s
wire:    replay result: <timeout or refused> (the kernel answered, not the app)
```

### Discussion

The demo drives three decision inputs and one enforcement leg. The CRS payload
prints the S2 negative-security verdicts. The BOLA case prints the S3
positive-security record. The `cel` leg prints the S3 rate rule over the same
view — the scoring input the ban ladder reads. The `ban` leg seeds one source ban through the loader ABI. A `BanVal` carries tier, reason code and a monotonic deadline. The value lands in the kernel map. The replay through the same flow dies in
TC before userspace (`TC_ACT_SHOT`).

The thresholds and tiers live in [spec §13.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#133-the-ban-algorithm-scoredwindowban-v1-specified).
This recipe drives the enforcement leg and the map evidence; the full decider
census reads in the same section.

### See also

- [spec §13](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#13-rate-limiting-dos-response--temporary-bans) — rate limits, DoS, bans. [spec §13.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#133-the-ban-algorithm-scoredwindowban-v1-specified) — ScoredWindowBan.
- [`docs/demo.md`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/demo.md) — the demo's honesty table.
- [Issue #83](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/83) — the recorded attack-demo transcripts.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, inside the sprint Linux VM (kernel `7.0.14-orbstack-00380`, bpftool v7.4.0):

- The demo ran exit 0 at the pin. The program loaded and attached on the veth pair; the four maps pinned.
- The ban row landed in the map (`family=4 class=0 tier=1 reason=4211`). The replay after the ban
  read the kernel answer, not the app.

## Recipe 7 — Pre-seed the kernel maps from the operator bundle

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`test/route-e2e`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/test/route-e2e), Linux VM, root, BTF | Kernel · operator | hard | 10 min | kernel · lpm | bundle, route class, verifier |

### Problem

You want the bundle's kernel leg loaded before traffic. You want the route-class
LPM rows from the compiled policy.

### Solution

1. Run the route E2E (root, Linux, BTF present). `ROUTE_E2E_REQUIRED=1` turns
every environment skip into a failure:

```bash
sudo env PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" ROUTE_E2E_REQUIRED=1 \
  go test -tags route_e2e -count=1 -v ./test/route-e2e/
```

2. Read the load proof. The suite compiles the full pathway and loads it under
the kernel verifier:

```text
=== RUN   TestRouteClassLoadProofE2E
--- PASS: TestRouteClassLoadProofE2E (<seconds>s)
--- PASS: TestBundleShapeLoadGate (<seconds>s)
--- PASS: TestBundleShapeGateNegatives (<seconds>s)
PASS
```

### Discussion

The pathway runs end to end. `WAFPolicy` compiles to a bundle. The bundle instantiates one verifier-accepted route-mark program with one LPM map. The map carries the compiled route prefixes as the pre-seeded rows. No
netns and no traffic attach ride this proof: the gate is the verifier load plus
the read-back. The census stamps each policy field kernel or slow path; the
census record defines the boundary.

The bundle shapes walk as a contract. A bundle that loses its kernel leg fails before the verifier sees it.

### See also

- [spec §16.4](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#164-lifecycle-of-trishula-in-a-cluster) — the lifecycle of Trishula in a cluster.
- [`docs/design/socket-plane/4-compiler-census.md`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/design/socket-plane/4-compiler-census.md) — the census boundary.
- [TR-40b issue #188](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/188) — the route-class end-to-end lane.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, inside the sprint Linux VM (kernel `7.0.14-orbstack-00380`):

- `ROUTE_E2E_REQUIRED=1 go test -tags route_e2e -count=1 -v ./test/route-e2e/`: exit 0.
  `TestRouteClassLoadProofE2E`, `TestBundleShapeLoadGate`, `TestBundleShapeGateNegatives` all PASS.

## Recipe 8 — Run the CRS differential and the bench harness on your own node

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/bench-vm.sh`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/bench-vm.sh) + [`test/crs-differential`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/test/crs-differential), Linux VM, root | Bench | hard | 45 min | bench · crs | bench, budgets, walls |

### Problem

You want the full suite under the CI shape on the node you own. You want the
verdict walls measured against the [spec §17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#17-performance-targets--benchmark-plan)
budgets, and the CRS posture re-checked on the same node.

### Solution

1. Run the CRS parity gate first (any host with Go):

```bash
go test ./test/crs-differential/ -run TestCorpusParity -count=1
```

2. Run the bench rig inside a Linux VM copy of the tree (root):

```bash
sudo bash lab/bench-vm.sh
```

3. Read the four sections the rig prints:

```text
== G: full suite, new CI shape (p 1 + no_regex_multiline)
== H: old CI shape control (parallel, GOMAXPROCS=4)
== I: bench verdict walls, new CI shape
== J: prefilter-off control (same shape, directive removed)
```

The wall lines carry one row per measured scenario:

```text
MEASURED <scenario> n=<n> size=<bytes> p50=<us> p99=<us> budget=<name> (<budget-hint us>) factor=<x>x
```

### Discussion

Section G runs the suite serialized (`-p 1`) with the `no_regex_multiline` build
tag; the CI fleet runs this shape. Section H runs the parallel-shape control;
the delta shows what the serialization buys. Section I measures the live-path verdict walls against the named budget. The `factor` value reads the wall at 1.00x. Section J removes the `SecRxPreFilter On`
directive and re-measures; the delta prices the prefilter. The rig restores the
directive on exit.

A wall above 1.00x is a budget miss on your node. The hosted CI certifies the
budgets; read the VM as the A and B surface. The parity gate from Recipe 5 rides
the same tree: run it again after any rule or exclusion change.

### See also

- [spec §17](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#17-performance-targets--benchmark-plan) — the budgets and the benchmark plan. [spec §11.8](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#118-crs-differential-parity-gate) — the parity gate.
- [The lab bench recipe](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/README.md) — the lab surfaces.
- [TR-24 issue #24](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/24) — the bench harness lane.
- Recipe 5 above — the same parity gate with the exclusion probes.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, inside the sprint Linux VM:

- The parity gate read green before the rig.
- `bash lab/bench-vm.sh` ran the four sections inside the VM. The section I wall read
  `MEASURED attack-sqli-small n=300 size=17 B p50=427.3 us p99=571.5 us budget=e2e-inline-hop-8k (1500 us) factor=0.38x`
  against the `e2e-inline-hop-8k` budget.
